title: Periodic Valuation of a Keyturn Vehicle Listing and Movement between Value Classes
content:
The marketplace values every live vehicle again at the class's refresh interval, counted in whole calendar days from the date of the last valuation, and the valuation it arrives at governs the class the vehicle sits in.

The refresh is due once the number of whole calendar days the class publishes has passed since the date of the valuation standing on the vehicle's condition record, that date being taken from the record and not from the host's recollection, and the vehicle being identified by the listing the valuation was filed against. The comparison is a not-earlier-than: the day on which the interval is exactly reached satisfies it.

*On the boundary.* A class whose refresh interval is 365 calendar days, the valuation standing on the record dated the anchor day: on the day 365 calendar days after that date the refresh is due; on the day before it is not yet due.

Where the fresh valuation puts the vehicle outside the band of the class it is listed in, the listing is moved into the class the valuation names, and the move takes effect on the date the valuation is recorded rather than on the next trip.

A host who disagrees puts the vehicle to a value class review, and the review takes the class's review period in business days; the vehicle stays in its existing class while the review runs, so trips already booked are unaffected.

**Clause withdrawn.** "A host's own declared value is accepted where it sits inside the class's tolerance of the marketplace valuation, and where it sits outside, the marketplace valuation governs and the host is told what the vehicle has been valued at." That clause is no longer in force on a Keyturn Vehicle Listing and is not to be applied; what the host's own declared value does to the value that governs the listing is settled on the current basis for settling the governing value. The class tolerance keeps its standing as a published figure of the class.

Moving up a class requires the settled trip count the target class sets, so a vehicle is not lifted into a higher class on valuation alone; moving down a class carries no such requirement, because a vehicle that has lost value must be priced and protected accordingly.

**Clause withdrawn.** "A class change moves the price floor and ceiling with it, and a daily price outside the new class's band is brought to the nearer boundary rather than left outside it." That clause is no longer in force on a Keyturn Vehicle Listing and is not to be applied; what a fresh valuation does to the daily price is settled on the current basis for setting the daily price.

A class change moves the price floor and ceiling with it, and a daily price outside the new class's band is brought to the nearer boundary rather than left outside it.
